P10-004.boundary_rationale: Onset side: 40:20 opens the outer court's gate circuit on a measure notice rather than a vayiqtol verb, מָדַ֥ד אָרְכּ֖וֹ וְרָחְבּֽוֹ (oshb:Ezek.40.20) 'he measured its length and its width', immediately after the outer court's whole-court span closes at 40:19. P10-004.strongest_rejected_alternative: The strongest rival is a cut at 40:23/40:24, weighed here face by face. Its near face, 40:24, opens the outer south gate on a transport verb (oshb:Ezek.40.24) and is a transport verse of the counted class (sweep: 33 verses / 46 occurrences), a licensed driver inside the vision; its far face, 40:23, ends the outer north gate on the hundred cubits measured from gate to gate (oshb:Ezek.40.23), with no formula and no mark. The cut leaves 40:20-23 and 40:24-27 at four verses each, so neither side falls under three verses and no length ground holds against it. The row holds on a stated ground: the outer court's north and south gates stand together as one measured block, and the verb at 40:24 only turns the tour toward another compass point inside the same outer court, whereas this row's own edges are larger turns in the survey, the whole-court measure closing at 40:19 behind it and the court-change transport at 40:28 ahead of it.
